findings.description: In _run, the except branch sets job.next_run = now + self._retry_delay(job) (line 65), but the finally block then unconditionally sets job.next_run = now + job.interval (line 76). finally runs after except, so the retry schedule is always discarded. A failing job is rescheduled after its full interval instead of the intended retry_delay, and the exponential backoff is dead code. Failures that would be retried within a minute are delayed by a whole interval, for example a day for daily_at jobs.
findings.suggestion: Remove the finally block and restore a single assignment after the try/except/else, for example set job.next_run = now + job.interval in the else branch and now + self._retry_delay(job) in the except branch.
findings.title: finally overwrites the retry delay, so failed jobs never back off

findings.description: consecutive_failures is unbounded and max_failures can be set arbitrarily high. With 2 ** (consecutive_failures - 1) growing, job.retry_delay * 2**n eventually exceeds timedelta's maximum (around 2**41 minutes-scale multiples), raising OverflowError. That exception is raised inside the except block of _run, so it escapes tick() and prevents the remaining due jobs in that tick from running, and the job is never disabled.
findings.suggestion: Cap the exponent or cap the result before multiplying, for example compare consecutive_failures against a bound derived from interval/retry_delay or compute the delay in seconds with a clamped exponent.
findings.title: Backoff exponent can overflow timedelta and raise from inside the failure handler
